# Vertical overlay: Dams

**Level:** CISA critical infrastructure sector (child of NAICS 22 Utilities)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 221111 Hydroelectric Power Generation. Hydroelectric generating station operating a regulated dam.
**Primary system:** Hydro plant control and dam monitoring system

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
SRMA: Department of Homeland Security (CISA); FERC Division of Dam Safety and Inspections (non-federal hydropower licensees); U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (federal dams/levees); Bureau of Reclamation (federal dams); NERC (hydro generators meeting BES criteria)

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**FERC Security Program for Hydropower Projects (Rev. 3A)**, FERC D2SI Security Program, incl. Section 9 cyber/SCADA and Form 3 Cyber Security Inspection Checklist. The only dam-specific federal security program with explicit cyber/SCADA requirements, inspected by FERC D2SI. Hydro generators that are BES assets must also meet NERC CIP; federal (USACE/USBR) dams follow internal federal (FISMA) controls instead.
Source: https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-04/security.pdf

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** CEII (dam inundation maps, design data; 18 CFR 388.113); Vulnerability/Security Assessments and Security Plans; PCII; BES Cyber System Information (for BES hydro)
- **Critical systems:** Spillway and gate control PLCs; Hydro unit control/governor systems; SCADA and remote control centers for multiple projects; Dam safety instrumentation and early-warning systems; Levee pump station controls
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** None identified beyond cross-sector obligations
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** None noted
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Unauthorized access to spillway and turbine control systems
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** Dam-safety sensor anomaly detection

## Notes
CIRCIA NPRM has no dams-specific sector criterion; hydro owners are covered via NERC CIP/OE-417 criterion or size standard.
